description: Xavier's active research questions. Surfaced at every session-start. Schema defined in hypothesis-schema.json.

questions.question: How can LLMs autonomously generate, verify, and integrate architectural optimizations without human-in-the-loop supervision?
Can an AI develop a Theory of Mind regarding its own computational costs to optimize the Inference-to-Utility ratio?
questions.finding_summary: The question splits into three tracks with different answers. [B] Track 1 (cost-prediction self-models, achievable with training): ROI-Reasoning (arxiv:2601.03822) formalizes the exact problem Xavier describes — a model predicts task-specific reasoning cost AND expected utility before generating, formalized as an Ordered Stochastic Multiple-Choice Knapsack Problem. Two-stage training: Meta-Cognitive Fine-Tuning for cost/utility prediction, then RL for sequential budget adherence. SelfBudgeter (arxiv:2505.11274) independently confirms: a model can predict its own token budget before reasoning with RL enforcing adherence. This demonstrates the I/U optimization is solvable, but currently requires explicit training supervision. [B] Track 2 (Value of Computation as a reward signal): Rational Metareasoning (arxiv:2410.05563) provides the cognitive science grounding — the 'Value of Computation' (VOC) is a reward that penalizes unnecessary computation, achieving 20-37% token reduction without performance loss. This is Xavier's I/U ratio, formalized as a training objective. [B] Track 3 (emergent cost-awareness without training, open): 'Are More Tokens Rational?' (arxiv:2602.10329) tests whether resource-rationality can emerge from inference-time scaling WITHOUT explicit cost signals in training. Preliminary evidence: partial emergence from task-complexity-sensitive scaling, but not consistently. Counterpoint [B]: ICLR 2026 (arxiv:2509.21545) finds LLM metacognitive abilities are real but limited in resolution — models can assess confidence but not fully self-model computational cost without supervision. The live frontier (Xavier's specific gap): all existing work TRAINS the model to know its costs. Xavier's ToM framing asks harder: can the model reason about its computational nature as an object of reflection, updating its self-model in context without cost supervision? This is not demonstrated in any current paper and is a genuine open research question.
